Recovery archives damaged bytes, trusted pending JSON and disabled-task XML with create-only writes/readback before replacing state. It rechecks hashes and observed task/resource state under installer/controller mutexes and again immediately before retirement. No network mutation or task enable operation is present.

Limits: No power-cut, storage-controller persistence or directory-metadata durability qualification. Flush API use is not proof against hardware power loss.

Mutexes coordinate cooperating installer/controller/recovery participants. Hash-before-Move is not atomic compare-and-swap against arbitrary privileged writers. Trusted administrator-controlled paths and declarations remain prerequisites.

Portable/inert provider tests do not qualify live hardware, actual task scheduler behavior, deployed controller identity or real retirement; root must bind and recheck its read-only plan before live Apply.
